comments.text: Hi everyone, I'm Elle, and I work on product and go-to-market for zCAD. The question we kept coming back to: where is this model going to live? If it lives in a game, a render or a virtual world, a mesh is the right answer, and AI 3D tools already do it well. If it has to work in the physical world, fit another part, take a screw, get printed or machined, it needs CAD: real dimensions, solid geometry, parts that mate. zCAD. AI generates that from a prompt, and exports STEP into the tool you already use.On the product side, a few choices are deliberate. Even the free plan exports STEP, because a part you can't take into your own tools isn't really yours. We turn down figurine requests, because sculpted, organic shapes are what mesh does best, even when you print them. And it doesn't make engineering calls for you. Tolerances and materials stay with you. On the go-to-market side, I'll be honest: we're still learning who needs this most. Makers who 3D print, indie hardware designers, engineers who live in CAD all day? That's a big part of why we're here. Try it on something that has to work in the real world, and tell us who you are and where it breaks.

comments.text: Hi everyone, I'm Martín, an indie macOS developer (I also make Tangible). I built Many Displays because my two identical LG 4K monitors swapped places after every sleep, and every window piled up on one of them. macOS can't tell identical monitors apart because many ship with the same EDID serial, and DisplayPort monitors "disconnect" when the Mac sleeps. Many Displays keeps one layout per combination of displays. It tells identical monitors apart by system UUID and then by physical port, fixes the arrangement, resolution, rotation and HDR first, and then puts every window back by itself. It reads the window server's list (about 20 ms for hundreds of windows) instead of asking every app through Accessibility, so a busy app never stalls it. No network, no analytics, and the source is on GitHub under the FSL (MIT after two years). It's $19 one-time with a year of updates, after a 14-day trial with no account. I'd love to hear about setups where it fails: docks, three or more monitors, odd Spaces configs.

yesterday.description: MOVO AI is the world’s first AI video agent for long-form creation that works right from your phone. It also works on the web. comments.text: Hi Product Hunt 👋I’m one of the makers behind MOVO AI—the world’s first long-form video agent on your mobile.My mother is a small creator who manages several social media accounts, and my father is her loyal cameraman. They are both over 60, but they still spend hours filming, editing, posting, and proudly watching every new like and follower.They make little, if any, money from it. But social media gives them something real: an audience, confidence, and the feeling that their stories are being seen.At the same time, I watched more founders around me become creators. They recorded videos between meetings, explained their ideas to customers, and built influence around themselves and their products.I was different. I was an introverted engineer who began working in AI while completing my graduate degree at Carnegie Mellon University. I had ideas, but I didn’t understand camera movements, editing, or how to look natural on camera. Even with the newest iPhone, I often didn’t know where to begin.My parents showed me how meaningful it could be to share your life. The founders around me showed me how necessary video was becoming. Together, they made me feel like I was being left behind by an era I was helping to build.That gap became the reason we built MOVO AI.What is MOVO?MOVO turns an idea into a complete long-form video through one continuous conversation.Start with a rough thought, script, reference, or a few assets. MOVO helps structure the story, establish the characters and visual direction, generate scenes, respond to feedback, and compose everything into a cohesive video.You don’t need to know the technical name of every shot or write a complex prompt for each scene. You can simply talk to MOVO as you would talk to a director, creative partner, or friend.Internally, we describe it as “Codex for video”: you direct what you want to create without writing every underlying instruction yourself.What surprised usWe initially thought eliminating prompt gymnastics would mainly help beginners. Professional AI creators already knew how to write sophisticated prompts, select models, and manage complicated workflows.We underestimated how much professionals would value this approach too.They embraced it not because they couldn’t write prompts, but because they wanted to focus their attention on what matters more: story, structure, pacing, characters, and emotion.Conversations with accomplished professors and screenwriters at USC’s School of Cinematic Arts reinforced this belief. Models and production tools will keep changing, but storytelling remains the foundation.We realized that agentic creation is not simply an easier mode for beginners. It may be a more universal creative interface: accessible enough for a first-time creator, yet powerful enough to free professionals from repetitive production work.Why mobile mattersOnce creation becomes conversational, it no longer needs to live inside a desktop canvas.A founder can start a product video before the next meeting. A store owner can review an advertisement from behind the counter. A parent can develop a family story in the park. A filmmaker can approve scenes while moving between locations. A hiker can capture an idea at the summit before the inspiration disappears.You might describe an idea over breakfast, approve the storyboard on the train, review generated scenes after work, and refine the ending before bed.MOVO continues working asynchronously, so you don’t need to babysit every generation. Creation can move with your life instead of requiring your life to stop.From one video to an ongoing worldWithin the same project, you can begin Episodes 2, 3, and 4 in new sessions without re-entering the same characters, products, locations, and creative direction.MOVO carries that context forward, helping you develop an ongoing world rather than a collection of disconnected clips.What we’d love you to testWe would especially value feedback on three things:Does talking to MOVO feel like working with a useful director or creative partner?Can you meaningfully develop a video on mobile without supervising every step?How well does MOVO preserve your creative world across multiple episodes?AI video still has many unsolved problems, and MOVO is still evolving. We want to hear where it understands your direction, where it surprises you, and where it falls short.Our goal is not to replace human creativity. It is to close the gap between having a story and being able to show it.Anyone with a story should be able to make it move—wherever life takes them.Your idea. Moved by MOVO. 🎬

comments.text: Eleven Realtime is ElevenLabs’ new family of speech-to-speech models for building voice agents that sound natural in conversation.Problem: Voice agents are usually stitched together from separate parts: speech recognition, a language model, turn-taking logic and a voice. Each hand-off adds delay, and that’s where conversations start to feel stiff, with awkward pauses and talking over each other.Solution: Eleven Realtime tunes speech recognition, turn-taking, the LLM and the voice end to end. It comes in two models. v1 Mini is built for natural conversation, and v1 Max is built for complex tasks that need precise, deliberate answers. You can use it in ElevenAgents or through a Realtime API.What makes it different: The API is OpenAI-compatible, so if you already have a voice app built on OpenAI’s Realtime API, you change the endpoint and model name and your existing event handlers keep working. Per ElevenLabs, time to first audio is 620 ms for v1 Mini and 570 ms for v1 Max, across 90+ languages.Key features:v1 Mini for assistants, tutors and interactive charactersv1 Max for lead qualification, customer support and schedulingPick the model from one dropdown in ElevenAgents, with transcription, turn-taking and voice preconfiguredDeploy to phone, web widget, WhatsApp and contact center platformsKnowledge base, guardrails, scripted scenario testing and production monitoring in ElevenAgentsSearchable, auditable conversation logsPer ElevenLabs, SOC 2, HIPAA and GDPR support, with EU Data Residency and Zero Retention modesWho it’s for: Developers and teams building voice agents for support, sales, scheduling or education who want natural-sounding conversations without wiring the pieces together themselves.Try it via Eleven Realtime, the docs and the OpenAI compatibility guide.

yesterday.name: Cloudflare Clairic
yesterday.tagline: Cloudflare's AI model for fast, cheap data extraction
yesterday.description: Clairic is Cloudflare's new AI model for extracting structured information without generating tokens. Give it messy text or images, and it returns typed values like names, dates, amounts, calculations, and estimates in a single pass, with confidence scores. Built for developers who need faster, cheaper data processing than traditional LLM calls. Available in preview on Workers AI at $0.10 per million input tokens, with open weights planned.

comments.text: Cloudflare just released Clairic, and I think the idea behind it is pretty interesting. We're using LLMs for all sorts of tasks that don't really need text generation — extracting invoice totals, reading dates, pulling information from documents, etc. Clairic is built specifically for that kind of work. It returns structured values in a single pass, without generating tokens one by one. It's also just $0.10 per million input tokens on Workers AI. Still an early preview, but I'm curious to see how these smaller, specialized models change the way we build AI applications.

year.tagline: The inbox designed for humans and agents
year.description: Finally, an inbox you'll look forward to. Agents sort your messages, draft your replies, and clear the grunt work behind the scenes, all in a client so well-crafted that email feels light, fast, fun.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! 👋 Louis here, co-founder of Upstream.When I was at Algolia, I was drowning in 200 emails a day. I was never sure where to focus, and getting through my inbox took forever. I knew it didn’t have to be this way. Instead of creating a new messaging protocol, I bet on rethinking the tool everyone uses: email.We built the first email client where agents do real work alongside people. We designed Upstream to be easy to pick up and fun to use. 📥 Take the noise out of emailAgents automatically triage your inbox, separate signal from noise, and surface only what deserves your attention✍️ Every reply starts with a draftUpstream drafts replies for every conversation that needs one. It also changes your voice based on who you’re talking to and the context of the convo⏰ Never miss a follow-upAgents track open loops and remind you when needed, making sure important conversations don't fall through the cracks🔎 Ask anything about your workAI can instantly find information across your inbox and connected tools: receipts, meeting notes, introductions, decisions, conversations, and more🔗 Bring all your context into your inboxAgents use information from tools like Notion, Calendar, Drive, Granola, and other sources to produce better answers and drafts👉 As a special thank you to the Product Hunt community, you get one free month of Upstream Pro if you sign up at upstream.do and use the code PH26! 👈We are all so excited to hear what you think!
